content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Ogden

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years. Verify your education and hours logged on active projects meet PMI's standards before enrolling in formal training.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP course. Attend sessions online on a schedule that fits your work commitments. Earn your 35 required contact hours and receive your certificate of completion to submit with your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Complete your PMP application directly with PMI, reporting your education, project experience, and training completion. Pay the PMI examination fee and wait for approval. Most applications are reviewed within five business days.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, including practice questions and study guides, to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your computer-based exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. Pass the 180-question assessment to earn your PMP credential.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: Earn professional development units (PDUs) over a three-year cycle to renew your PMP. Pursue continuing education, volunteer work, or authorship in project-management disciplines. Renew your certification before expiration to keep your credential active.
